newsitem.title: CHINA: China bans new all-foreign polyester projects.
newsitem.headline: China bans new all-foreign polyester projects.

text.p: China has banned the creation of new polyester projects that are solely funded or controlled by foreigners, saying the industry should expand output at existing plants, official media said on Tuesday.

China would boost polyester output capacity and cut down on imports of the chemical fibre, which could help ease demand for cotton in the textile industry, the China Daily quoted a State Planning Commission official as saying.

The government would encourage more investment in polyester production, including foreign investment and joint investment by different local authorities, the newspaper quoted commission official Feng Wenying as saying.
But the Xinhua news agency quoted a commission official as saying foreign investment would face restrictions.
"China will approve no more polyester manufacturing firms which are solely funded or controlled by foreigners," Xinhua quoted the official as saying in a report late Monday night.
"China needs more polyester, but will get it only by expanding current output rather than launching new ones," said the official, whom Xinhua did not name.
The industry should boost annual polyester output to three million tonnes while reducing imports, the China Daily quoted Feng as saying.
Polyester production capacity was 1.9 million tonnes in 1995, Feng said but gave no further details.
